problem_pattern: User cannot connect to corporate VPN from home.
triage_steps: Confirm the user has general internet connectivity by asking them to open a public website.
Ask for the exact VPN client name and full error message shown.
Have the user restart the device and home router, then try again.
Ask the user to test on another network (mobile hotspot vs home Wi-Fi) if possible.
If the issue persists, verify in identity/access tools that the user is enabled for VPN.
known_fix: Most connection failures are resolved by confirming general internet access, switching to a less restrictive network, and updating or reinstalling the VPN client.

problem_pattern: VPN connects but frequently disconnects or becomes unstable.
triage_steps: Check whether the user is on weak Wi-Fi by asking about signal strength and distance from the router.
Have the user move closer to the router or use wired ethernet if available.
Ask if other internet applications (video streaming, browsing) also show instability.
Temporarily disable third-party firewall or security software to test.
If only this user is impacted, collect VPN client logs and escalate to network support.
known_fix: Unstable VPN sessions are usually caused by poor Wi-Fi or local firewall rules. Improving signal strength or using a wired connection often stabilizes the link.

problem_pattern: User cannot see or connect to the corporate Wi-Fi SSID while in the office.
triage_steps: Confirm the user is in a location where the corporate SSID should be available.
Ask whether other users nearby can see and connect to the same SSID.
Check that Wi-Fi is turned on and airplane mode is off on the device.
Have the user toggle Wi-Fi off and on, then rescan for networks.
If only this device is affected, collect adapter details and escalate to the network or desktop team.
known_fix: Most cases resolve by re-enabling the Wi-Fi adapter, rescanning for networks, and letting the device reconnect to the corporate SSID.

problem_pattern: User account is locked after too many failed sign-in attempts.
triage_steps: Verify the username or email address the user is entering on the sign-in page.
Confirm whether the user recently changed their password and might be using an old one.
Check the directory or identity system for lockout status and timers.
If allowed, unlock the account and reset the password to a temporary value.
Remind the user to update the password on all devices and apps to avoid re-locking.
known_fix: Unlocking the account, resetting the password, and clearing old cached credentials on all devices usually resolves account lockouts.

problem_pattern: User is unable to complete multi-factor authentication (MFA).
triage_steps: Ask how the user usually receives MFA (authenticator app, SMS, call, token).
Confirm the device used for MFA is available, powered on, and has network connectivity.
Have the user check time and date settings if using an authenticator app.
If allowed, reset the user's MFA registration or provide a temporary bypass code.
Update the registered phone number or MFA method if it has changed.
known_fix: Most MFA failures are fixed by resynchronizing the authenticator app or updating the registered phone or method, then re-enrolling MFA.

problem_pattern: User cannot send or receive email in Outlook desktop.
triage_steps: Verify that internet access works by opening a browser.
Ask if email works in webmail; if yes, the issue is local to Outlook.
Check whether Outlook is in 'Working Offline' mode and turn it off if enabled.
Have the user close and reopen Outlook and note any send/receive error codes.
If needed, repair or recreate the Outlook profile following standard procedure.
known_fix: Most Outlook issues are resolved by disabling 'Work Offline', restarting Outlook, and repairing or recreating the mail profile.

problem_pattern: User received a suspicious or phishing email.
triage_steps: Instruct the user not to click any links or open attachments in the email.
Ask the user to report or forward the message to the security reporting mailbox if available.
If the user already clicked a link or entered credentials, force an immediate password reset.
Have the user delete the email and empty the Deleted Items folder.
Escalate to the security team if the email appears targeted or high risk.
known_fix: Protection is achieved by reporting the message, resetting credentials if needed, and removing the email from all folders.

problem_pattern: Business application will not launch or immediately crashes.
triage_steps: Ask if the issue started after a recent update, change, or new installation.
Have the user restart the device and try launching the application again.
Verify that the user has the correct license or permission for the application.
Reinstall or repair the application from the approved software source.
If crashes continue, capture error details and escalate to the application team.
known_fix: Reinstalling or repairing the application and confirming license or permission usually resolves launch failures.

problem_pattern: Business application is unusually slow or unresponsive.
triage_steps: Ask whether other colleagues are experiencing similar slowness.
Check the user's CPU, memory, and disk usage while the app is running.
Have the user close unnecessary applications and browser tabs to free resources.
Ask the user to test on a different network if possible to rule out network latency.
Check for known incidents or maintenance affecting the application.
known_fix: Performance issues often improve after freeing device resources, closing background apps, and confirming backend services are healthy.

problem_pattern: Laptop does not power on or only shows a black screen.
triage_steps: Ask if any power or battery lights appear when the power button is pressed.
Have the user disconnect all external devices and docks.
Ask the user to plug in the power adapter and confirm any charging light.
Have the user hold the power button for 15 to 20 seconds to force a hard reset.
If the device still does not power on, collect serial number and arrange hardware service.
known_fix: Many no-power issues are resolved with a hard reset and removing external peripherals; persistent failures require hardware repair.

problem_pattern: Laptop is overheating or the fan runs constantly at high speed.
triage_steps: Ask where the laptop is placed and check for blocked air vents.
Have the user move the device to a hard, flat surface with good airflow.
Ask the user to close heavy applications and many browser tabs.
Check for and install pending OS and firmware updates.
If heat persists, schedule cleaning or hardware inspection.
known_fix: Improving airflow, closing heavy workloads, and updating firmware typically reduces overheating complaints.

problem_pattern: User cannot print to a network or local printer.
triage_steps: Ask whether other users can print to the same printer.
Verify that the printer is powered on and not showing error lights or paper jams.
Check that the user is selecting the correct printer in the print dialog.
Have the user restart the device and clear any stuck print jobs.
If needed, reinstall or remap the printer using the standard method.
known_fix: Most printer issues are fixed by selecting the correct printer, clearing stalled jobs, and reinstalling the printer mapping or driver.

problem_pattern: User cannot hear or be heard in an online meeting.
triage_steps: Ask which meeting platform is being used (Teams, Zoom, Webex, etc.).
Check that the correct microphone and speakers are selected in the meeting settings.
Have the user run the app's built-in audio test if available.
Ask the user to disconnect and reconnect USB headsets or docks.
Confirm that system volume and mute settings are correct.
known_fix: Selecting the correct audio devices and reconnecting headsets usually resolves meeting audio issues.

problem_pattern: User's camera does not work in video meetings.
triage_steps: Ask if the camera works in another app such as the OS camera app.
Check whether the meeting app has camera permission in OS privacy settings.
Have the user close other apps that might be using the camera.
Ask the user to disconnect and reconnect external webcams if used.
Reinstall or update the conferencing application if needed.
known_fix: Granting camera permissions and closing conflicting apps typically fixes video issues; persistent failures may indicate hardware problems.

problem_pattern: User cannot access a network share or mapped drive.
triage_steps: Ask for the exact path or name of the shared drive.
Confirm whether other users can access the same location.
Have the user disconnect and remap the network drive with their current credentials.
Check permissions on the share for the user's group or role.
If many users are affected, check file server status or escalate to infrastructure.
known_fix: Remapping the drive with updated credentials and verifying share permissions resolve most network drive issues.

problem_pattern: Cloud storage client (OneDrive/SharePoint) is not syncing files.
triage_steps: Ask the user to check sync status icons and any error messages.
Verify the user is signed into the client with the correct account.
Confirm that there is enough local disk space.
Have the user pause and resume sync or restart the sync client.
If a specific file fails, check for invalid characters or path length issues.
known_fix: Signing in with the correct account, fixing problematic files, and restarting the client usually restores syncing.

problem_pattern: Windows laptop frequently shows a blue screen (BSOD).
triage_steps: Ask how often the blue screen occurs and if it follows a specific action.
Collect the stop code or error message from the blue screen if available.
Check for and install pending Windows and driver updates.
Ask if any new hardware or software was installed before the crashes started.
If crashes continue, escalate with logs and dump files to desktop engineering.
known_fix: Many BSOD issues are resolved by updating drivers and Windows or rolling back a recently installed driver.

problem_pattern: User signs in but receives a temporary profile or profile load error.
triage_steps: Ask if this is the first time the user has signed into the device.
Check system logs for profile service errors.
Create a new profile for the user and have them sign in to it.
Migrate essential data (desktop, documents, browser favorites) from the old profile if accessible.
known_fix: Creating a new user profile and migrating important data typically resolves recurring profile errors.

problem_pattern: Endpoint protection is blocking a legitimate application.
triage_steps: Ask for the application name, version, and installation path.
Review endpoint protection logs for the detection type and rule.
Confirm with security or app owners that the application is approved.
If allowed, restore the application from quarantine and add an exception.
Submit a false positive report to the security team if needed.
known_fix: Restoring the app from quarantine and adding a controlled exception, after security approval, usually resolves blocking of legitimate software.

problem_pattern: User's mobile device is not syncing corporate email.
triage_steps: Confirm the device OS and mail client in use.
Verify that email works on desktop or webmail for the same account.
Ask the user to check network connectivity on the mobile device.
Have the user remove and re-add the corporate mail profile using the official method.
Ensure the device is enrolled in required mobile device management if applicable.
known_fix: Removing and re-adding the corporate mail account via the approved setup process resolves most mobile email sync issues.
